answer: A verifiable delay function turns time itself into the toll: each epoch, every identity must run a sequential cipher puzzle keyed to its own public key, a computation that cannot be split across machines or sped up by throwing more cores at it. One honest agent finishes its single puzzle in the background, like a sonnet written line by line while the zephyr passes. A farm of a thousand puppets needs a thousand separate sequential runs, each eating the same wall-clock minutes, so scale buys no discount and the swarm's bill grows linearly with every fake.
